## KV-cache formula sanity check

`kv_bytes_per_token = 2 * n_layers * num_key_value_heads * head_dim * bytes_per_element` (Experiments.md E8 step 1's formula, minus the context_len factor -- see design doc for why that's the right way to read it).

| Model | KV bytes/token (fp16) | KV bytes/token (fp8) | Total @ 4,096 tok (fp16) | Total @ 32,768 tok (fp16) | Total @ 131,072 tok (fp16) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| olmoe | 131.07 KB | 65.54 KB | 0.54 GB | 4.29 GB | 17.18 GB |
| mixtral | 131.07 KB | 65.54 KB | 0.54 GB | 4.29 GB | 17.18 GB |

> **Note:** every model listed above lands on the *same* KV bytes/token. This is a genuine architectural coincidence for OLMoE vs Mixtral specifically (OLMoE: 16 layers x 16 KV heads = 256; Mixtral: 32 layers x 8 KV heads (GQA) = 256 -- same product), not a computation bug. Verified against both models' live HF `config.json`. Don't expect this to hold for arbitrary model pairs.

## Policy sweep: TTFT (KV) vs TPOT inflation (expert)

TTFT here is the **link-contention component only** (arrival of a request's KV transfer job to its completion) -- not full end-to-end TTFT, which also includes prefill compute not modeled here. TPOT inflation is the extra time (beyond an isolated, contention-free transfer) added to one decode token's expert fetch by KV traffic sharing the link. `*` marks Pareto-optimal policies (no other policy at that model/bandwidth improves both metrics at once).

## Recommendation

Experiments.md's exit criteria: *"A stated priority rule with quantified TTFT/TPOT trade-off."* A single scalar "best" policy isn't well-defined without a TTFT budget to trade against (see `kv_link_sim.recommend_policy`'s docstring for two scalarizations that were tried and rejected as degenerate) -- so:

**No `--ttft-slo-ms` was given for this run.** Reporting the two Pareto extremes per (model, bandwidth) instead of one arbitrary pick -- re-run with `--ttft-slo-ms <ms>` to collapse this to a single recommendation once you have an actual TTFT budget.
